description: Comprehensive, research-backed catalog of production-readiness verification test cases for AI-built websites and applications.

categories.name: Authentication and Account Flows
categories.description: User registration, authentication, session lifecycle, token refresh, and account state transitions.

categories.name: Routing and Navigation
categories.description: Client and server route resolution, history navigation, deep links, guards, and 404 handling.

categories.name: Forms and Input Handling
categories.description: Client and server-side input validation, format constraints, submission idempotency, and error feedback.

categories.name: Core Business Logic and Data Integrity
categories.description: Data domain operations, arithmetic precision, data isolation, concurrency, and persistence guarantees.

categories.name: User Roles and Authorization
categories.description: Role-based access control, privilege boundaries, IDOR prevention, and tenant separation.

categories.name: API and Integration Reliability
categories.description: HTTP contract compliance, client/server error handling, rate limiting, and third-party outage tolerance.

categories.name: UI Quality and User Experience
categories.description: Interactive control responsiveness, state coverage (loading/empty/error), layout stability, and console hygiene.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.description: WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, keyboard navigation, focus management, semantic structure, and assistive technology support.

categories.name: Security
categories.description: OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, injection defense, XSS, CSRF, security headers, cookie flags, and secret isolation.

categories.name: Performance and Scalability
categories.description: Core Web Vitals, resource budgets, query optimization, memory leak prevention, and 100k capacity planning.

categories.name: Resilience and Reliability
categories.description: Service degradation, connection recovery, retry storms, graceful termination, and transactional integrity.

categories.name: Deployment and Production Configuration
categories.description: Production builds, environment variables, secret hygiene, migration execution, and release smoke testing.

categories.name: Search, Metadata, and Discoverability
categories.description: SEO metadata, canonical tags, crawler directives, social previews, structured data, and semantic statuses.

categories.name: Browser Compatibility and Network Behavior

categories.name: Observability and Post-Deployment Verification

test_cases.name: Login with valid credentials
test_cases.defect_target: Authentication failure, missing session establishment, or broken dashboard redirection for valid credentials
preconditions: A registered test user account exists in database/mock with known username/email and password
Authentication service is operational
steps: Navigate to the login view (/login)
Enter valid registered email/username into the credential field
Enter valid corresponding password into the password field
Submit the form via submit button or Enter key
Wait for authentication response and page redirect
test_cases.expected_result: Authentication request succeeds (HTTP 200/302), session cookie or auth token is securely stored, user is redirected to the intended destination view (e.g. /dashboard), and user profile is reflected in the UI
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use dedicated test user accounts; never use real production administrator or billing credentials.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Authentication and Session Management (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)
Playwright Authentication Documentation (https://playwright.dev/docs/auth)

test_cases.name: Login with invalid password
test_cases.defect_target: Authentication bypass with incorrect password, raw server error, or leakage of sensitive account state
preconditions: A registered test user account exists in database/mock
Authentication service is operational
steps: Navigate to the login view (/login)
Enter valid registered email/username
Enter an intentionally incorrect password (e.g. 'WrongPassword!999')
Submit the login form
Wait for server response and UI update
test_cases.expected_result: Authentication fails (HTTP 401), user remains on login view, a clear accessible error message is displayed (e.g. 'Invalid email or password'), password input is cleared or preserved without exposure, and no session token is granted
test_cases.safety_constraints: Ensure test account is not permanently locked out during automated regression runs if lockouts are enforced.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Generic Error Messages (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)
OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG-AUTHN-02)

test_cases.name: Login for nonexistent account
test_cases.defect_target: Account enumeration vulnerability, unhandled exception (500), or missing registration path for unregistered users
preconditions: Authentication service is operational
Test email/username is guaranteed not to exist in the database (e.g. 'nonexistent_user_99281@testdomain.invalid')
steps: Navigate to login view (/login)
Enter nonexistent email/username
Enter arbitrary password
Submit the form
test_cases.expected_result: Server returns standard unauthorized response (HTTP 401), displays neutral error message without distinguishing nonexistent username from invalid password (preventing enumeration), and presents an accessible link to the registration flow
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use reserved test domains like .invalid or .example for non-existent account tests.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Account Enumeration Defense (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Registration with valid input
test_cases.defect_target: Failure to create legitimate user accounts, missing confirmation/welcome state, or broken post-registration login/verification transition
preconditions: Self-registration is enabled in application configuration
Unique test email and compliant password prepared
steps: Navigate to registration view (/register or /signup)
Fill in valid username, unique email address, compliant password, and required confirmation fields
Accept terms of service if checkbox exists
Submit registration form
test_cases.expected_result: Account is successfully created (HTTP 201/200), user is either automatically logged in and redirected or presented with a clear verification/confirmation screen, and verification email dispatch is queued if enabled
test_cases.safety_constraints: Clean up created test user in test teardown or use an isolated staging test database.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Implement Proper Password Strength Controls (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Registration with invalid input and validation errors
test_cases.defect_target: Acceptance of weak passwords, malformed emails, or missing required profile fields during signup
preconditions: Registration view is accessible
steps: Navigate to registration view (/register)
Test scenario A: Enter malformed email (e.g. 'invalid-email-format')
Test scenario B: Enter weak password (e.g. '123' or 'password')
Test scenario C: Leave required confirmation field blank or mismatched
Submit form for each scenario
test_cases.expected_result: Submission is blocked client-side or rejected server-side (HTTP 400/422), clear accessible inline validation messages appear next to relevant fields with aria-invalid='true', and no account is created
test_cases.safety_constraints: Non-destructive; can be executed in any environment.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Password Strength Meter (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Duplicate account registration attempt
test_cases.defect_target: Creation of duplicate user identities, unhandled database unique constraint crash (500), or account overwrite
preconditions: An existing active user account with email 'registered_user@example.com' exists in database
steps: Navigate to registration view (/register)
Attempt to register a new account using 'registered_user@example.com'
Enter all other required fields validly and submit
test_cases.expected_result: Registration request is rejected cleanly (HTTP 400/409), database constraints prevent duplicate record insertion, and user is shown an accessible message indicating an account already exists with guidance to login or reset password
test_cases.safety_constraints: Do not delete or overwrite the existing pre-seeded test account.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Account Creation (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Password visibility toggle controls
test_cases.defect_target: Broken show/hide password buttons, inaccessible toggle without aria-label, or typed value clearing when toggling
preconditions: Login or registration form contains a password toggle control
steps: Navigate to login or register form
Type 'SecretP@ssw0rd!' into password field
Verify input attribute type is initially 'password'
Click the password visibility toggle button
Inspect input attribute type and rendered text
Verify toggle button aria-label updates appropriately (e.g. from 'Show password' to 'Hide password')
Click toggle again to re-mask password
test_cases.expected_result: Input type toggles between 'password' and 'text', typed characters remain intact without resetting or clearing, and toggle control maintains accessible name and keyboard operability
citations: Google web.dev - Sign-in form best practices (https://web.dev/articles/sign-in-form-best-practices)

test_cases.name: Forgot-password and password reset flow
test_cases.defect_target: Inability to recover account, token reuse vulnerability, token leak in URL logs, or failure to invalidate old sessions after reset
preconditions: A test user account exists with accessible mailbox or mock email trap
Password recovery mechanism is configured
steps: Navigate to /forgot-password
Submit registered email address
Retrieve generated reset token from mock email service / database
Navigate to /reset-password?token=<token>
Enter new compliant password and submit
Attempt to login with new password
Attempt to reuse the already-consumed reset token a second time
test_cases.expected_result: Password reset succeeds, user can login with new password, previous active sessions/tokens are invalidated, and consuming the reset token a second time returns an expired/invalid token error
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use mailhog or local mock SMTP; never spam real email addresses.
citations: OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Forgot_Password_Cheat_Sheet.html)
OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG-ATHN-09)

test_cases.name: Email verification flow
test_cases.defect_target: Unverified users accessing restricted verified-only features, or broken token verification link
preconditions: Newly registered user account with email_verified = false exists
Valid verification token generated
steps: Log in as unverified user and attempt to access verified-only action/route
Verify prompt/banner asking for email verification is shown
Navigate to verification URL with valid token (/verify-email?token=<token>)
Check database state and UI confirmation
Navigate to the previously blocked route
test_cases.expected_result: Token verification confirms account status, sets email_verified = true, displays success confirmation, and permits access to verified-only features
test_cases.safety_constraints: Ensure test verification tokens expire according to application security policy.
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Email Verification (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Logout and protected-route invalidation
test_cases.defect_target: Zombie session where cookies/tokens remain valid after logout, or protected page visible via browser back button
preconditions: User is currently logged in on a protected page (e.g. /dashboard)
steps: Click user menu and activate the logout button
Wait for logout API call and redirection to public page (/login or /)
Verify session cookies/tokens are cleared or invalidated on server
Attempt to navigate back to /dashboard via direct URL bar navigation
Attempt to click browser back button
test_cases.expected_result: Logout terminates session on server and client, direct navigation to /dashboard redirects to /login, and clicking back button does not render cached sensitive user data
citations: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet - Session Termination (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)
Playwright Authentication Guide (https://playwright.dev/docs/auth)

test_cases.name: Session persistence across page refresh and navigation
test_cases.defect_target: Session lost on browser page reload (F5) or navigation between internal links, forcing unexpected re-login
preconditions: User is logged in and viewing an authenticated dashboard page
steps: Log in to application
Navigate to a deep nested protected view (e.g. /dashboard/profile)
Trigger full browser page reload (F5 / page.reload())
Wait for network idle and DOM content loaded
Navigate to another protected tab/sub-route via navigation bar
test_cases.expected_result: Authenticated state persists seamlessly, user identity remains populated, no login prompt appears, and view renders with full authenticated privileges
citations: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Expired authentication token handling and silent refresh
test_cases.defect_target: Application crash, silent white screen, or infinite redirect loops when JWT or session token expires
preconditions: Authenticated session with expired token or mock network interceptor simulating HTTP 401 with token_expired code
steps: Simulate token expiration (either wait for short-lived token expiry or inject expired token in storage)
Trigger an authenticated API request or navigate to a protected page
Observe client-side interception behavior
If silent refresh is supported: verify refresh endpoint is called and session extended
If refresh fails or is unsupported: verify user is gracefully redirected to /login with return URL preserved
test_cases.expected_result: Application handles 401 token expiration gracefully without unhandled exception, attempts refresh if configured, otherwise redirects user to /login with notification explaining session expiration
test_cases.safety_constraints: Simulate expiry using mock tokens or network route interception to avoid long waits.
citations: OWASP JSON Web Token Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/JSON_Web_Token_for_Java_Cheat_Sheet.html)
Playwright Network Mocking Guide (https://playwright.dev/docs/network)

test_cases.name: Deep-link return URL redirect after login
test_cases.defect_target: User routed to default homepage after login rather than the specific protected deep link they initially attempted to access
preconditions: Unauthenticated browser context
Target protected deep link exists (e.g. /dashboard/reports/quarterly)
steps: Navigate directly to /dashboard/reports/quarterly while logged out
Verify redirect to /login with return URL encoded in query parameter (e.g. ?redirect=%2Fdashboard%2Freports%2Fquarterly)
Submit valid login credentials
Wait for post-authentication redirect
test_cases.expected_result: After successful authentication, user is redirected directly to the requested deep link (/dashboard/reports/quarterly) rather than a generic landing page
test_cases.safety_constraints: Verify redirect parameter sanitization to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities (covered in SEC-005).
citations: OWASP Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Unvalidated_Redirects_and_Forwards_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Multi-tab session synchronization on logout
test_cases.defect_target: Inconsistent state where logging out in Tab A leaves Tab B performing privileged actions with a dead session
preconditions: User is logged in across two simultaneous browser tabs in the same browser context
steps: Open Tab 1 and Tab 2, both navigated to /dashboard
In Tab 1, execute user logout
Switch to Tab 2 and attempt to trigger an action or refresh page
test_cases.expected_result: Tab 2 detects session termination via storage event/BroadcastChannel or API 401 response and redirects to /login or prompts for re-authentication without data corruption
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use a single browser context with multiple pages to test shared storage/cookies.
citations: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Rapid duplicate form submission prevention during auth
test_cases.defect_target: Multiple account creation requests dispatched, duplicate session records, or race condition crashes caused by double-clicking submit
preconditions: Registration or login form loaded in browser
steps: Fill valid credentials in login or registration form
Simulate network delay on auth endpoint (e.g. 1000ms delay)
Trigger rapid double-click or multiple clicks on submit button within 100ms
Inspect network panel request count
test_cases.expected_result: Submit button is immediately disabled or debounced, displays loading indicator, and exactly one network authentication request is dispatched to the backend
citations: Google web.dev - Sign-in form best practices (https://web.dev/articles/sign-in-form-best-practices)

test_cases.name: Direct loading of all top-level and nested routes
test_cases.defect_target: Route resolution crashes, blank screens, or 404 errors when visiting documented valid application paths directly
preconditions: Application frontend server or static build is serving routes
steps: Extract route table from router config (e.g. App.tsx, routes.ts, or page directory)
For each documented public or demo route, perform direct browser page.goto(url)
Inspect HTTP response status, document body, and console errors
test_cases.expected_result: Each route returns HTTP 200, renders intended main layout without white screen (root #app contains visible child elements), and produces zero fatal console errors
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Service Routing (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Direct refresh on nested SPA routes in deployed environment
test_cases.defect_target: Server returns 404 Not Found on browser reload of client-side nested routes (missing fallback/rewrite rule to index.html)
preconditions: Application deployed on web server (Nginx, Caddy, Vercel, Netlify, Cloud Run, S3/CloudFront)
steps: Navigate to a deep nested route (e.g. /app/items/123/details)
Issue a hard browser page reload bypassing client router cache (page.reload())
Inspect HTTP response status from web server
test_cases.expected_result: Web server rewrites request to index.html with HTTP 200, client-side router hydrates successfully, and target nested view renders correctly without web server 404 error
test_cases.safety_constraints: Non-destructive; critical for production deployment verification.
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Deployment Verification (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Browser history backward and forward navigation
test_cases.defect_target: Broken History API state, view failing to update on back/forward buttons, or lost scroll position
preconditions: Application running in browser
steps: Navigate from Route A (/home) to Route B (/products) by clicking a link
Navigate from Route B to Route C (/products/42) by clicking an item
Click browser Back button (page.goBack())
Verify view returns to Route B with active state
Click browser Forward button (page.goForward())
Verify view transitions back to Route C
test_cases.expected_result: Browser history stack maintains navigation sequence; forward and backward buttons restore respective route components and sync URL accurately
citations: MDN Web Docs - History API (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History_API)

test_cases.name: Unknown route handling and 404 page rendering
test_cases.defect_target: Crash, blank white screen, or raw unhandled router exception when a user visits a non-existent URL
preconditions: Application running in browser
steps: Navigate to an intentionally invalid route (e.g. /this-route-does-not-exist-at-all-404)
Wait for DOM render
Inspect rendered component and text content
Click the 'Return to Home' or equivalent recovery link on the 404 page
test_cases.expected_result: Application renders a friendly, branded 404 NotFound view (not a raw framework error or blank page), provides navigation link back to safety, and recovery link navigates successfully to home
citations: Google web.dev - Create useful 404 pages (https://web.dev/articles/search-console)

test_cases.name: Protected route redirection for unauthenticated visitors
test_cases.defect_target: Unauthorized visitor viewing private dashboard views, administrative panels, or settings screens without credentials
preconditions: Clean unauthenticated browser context (no cookies or tokens)
steps: Attempt to navigate directly to private routes (e.g. /dashboard, /account/billing, /admin)
Observe router guard response and URL changes
test_cases.expected_result: Router guard intercepts navigation before private data is fetched or rendered, redirects anonymous visitor to /login, and preserves target route in redirect query parameter
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Trailing slash and URL encoding consistency
test_cases.defect_target: Duplicate content, 404 errors, or broken route matchers caused by trailing slashes or encoded query characters
preconditions: Standard route with query parameter exists (e.g. /search?q=test%20query)
steps: Navigate to route with trailing slash (/about/)
Navigate to route without trailing slash (/about)
Navigate to route with encoded special characters in query string (/search?category=books%26media)
test_cases.expected_result: Both trailing slash variants resolve consistently to the same view or canonicalize via 301, and URL-encoded query parameters are decoded correctly without router crash
citations: Google Search Central - URL structure guidelines (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/url-structure)

test_cases.name: Redirect loop prevention in route guards
test_cases.defect_target: Infinite redirect loop (e.g. /login -> /onboarding -> /login -> ...) exhausting browser memory and blocking user
preconditions: Application has multiple conditional route guards (e.g. auth check, onboarding check, terms acceptance)
steps: Create test user in pending onboarding state
Navigate to /dashboard
Observe redirect behavior and monitor redirect count across 5 seconds
test_cases.expected_result: Redirect resolves to onboarding view in under 3 redirect hops without loop error (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS), and final page renders successfully
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use a browser timeout guard to catch infinite loops quickly.
citations: Playwright Network Guide - Handling Redirects (https://playwright.dev/docs/network)

test_cases.name: Internal link, breadcrumb, and navigation item integrity
test_cases.defect_target: Dead links (href='#', broken relative URLs, or missing target pages) in navbars, sidebars, footers, and breadcrumbs
preconditions: Application homepage and primary layout loaded
steps: Extract all internal <a> tags and button navigation triggers from header, sidebar, footer, and breadcrumbs
Validate that no link points to empty '#' or 'javascript:void(0)' unless designated as button component with key listener
Perform HEAD or GET check on each internal destination URL
test_cases.expected_result: All internal navigation links point to valid routes, return HTTP 200 (or expected redirect), and zero dead links exist across primary navigation chrome
test_cases.safety_constraints: Exclude external outbound links from automated crawl or test with HEAD only.
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Usability and Navigation (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Responsive mobile navigation drawer toggle and interaction
test_cases.defect_target: Hamburger button unclickable on mobile viewport, drawer failing to open/close, or links inside drawer unresponsive
preconditions: Browser viewport set to mobile dimensions (375x667 - iPhone SE / standard mobile)
steps: Set browser viewport to 375x667
Navigate to homepage
Locate and click hamburger menu toggle button
Verify mobile navigation drawer/modal is visible and aria-expanded='true'
Click an internal navigation link inside the drawer
Verify navigation occurs and drawer closes automatically
test_cases.expected_result: Mobile menu toggles open smoothly, traps or manages focus appropriately, selecting a link navigates to target route and dismisses the drawer without blocking screen
citations: Google web.dev - Responsive web design basics (https://web.dev/articles/responsive-web-design-basics)

test_cases.name: Required field validation and error association
test_cases.defect_target: Submitting incomplete forms, missing error messages, or error text not linked to input for screen readers
preconditions: Form view loaded in browser with one or more required fields
steps: Clear all required inputs in the form
Trigger form submission without typing values
Inspect input attributes and DOM for error containers
test_cases.expected_result: Submission is blocked, each invalid required input receives aria-invalid='true', clear error text is displayed, and error message is linked to input via aria-describedby
citations: W3C WAI Web Accessibility Tutorials - Form Validation (https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/validation/)

test_cases.name: Format and pattern validation for emails, numbers, and dates
test_cases.defect_target: Acceptance of malformed email addresses, negative numbers where prohibited, or impossible calendar dates
preconditions: Form containing email, numerical, or date inputs is rendered
steps: Enter invalid formatted values into targeted fields (e.g. 'plainaddress', 'abc' in price, '2026-02-31' in date)
Trigger field blur or form submission
Observe validation response
test_cases.expected_result: Inputs with invalid formats are flagged with specific guidance explaining the expected format (e.g. 'Please enter a valid email address'), and submission is prevented
citations: Google web.dev - Learn Forms: Validation (https://web.dev/learn/forms/validation/)

test_cases.name: Boundary value and maximum string length handling
test_cases.defect_target: Database column overflow error (500), buffer overflow, or UI truncation when typing maximum or oversized inputs
preconditions: Form with defined field length constraints (e.g. title max 100 chars, description max 1000 chars)
steps: Test scenario A: Enter input of exact maximum allowed length (N characters)
Test scenario B: Enter input exceeding maximum allowed length (N + 100 characters)
Submit form and verify database or API handling
test_cases.expected_result: Maximum length input succeeds without error; oversized input is either constrained by client maxlength attribute or rejected gracefully by backend with HTTP 422 and helpful message (no 500 error)
test_cases.safety_constraints: Clean up created boundary test records after execution.
citations: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Whitespace trimming and normalization
test_cases.defect_target: Accidental creation of accounts or records with leading/trailing spaces, or all-whitespace strings bypassing required checks
preconditions: Form with text input fields (e.g. name, email, search)
steps: Test A: Submit string composed solely of whitespace characters ('   ')
Test B: Submit valid email with accidental leading and trailing whitespace ('  test@example.com  ')
Inspect stored or processed value
test_cases.expected_result: All-whitespace string is rejected as empty for required fields; valid inputs have leading and trailing whitespace trimmed automatically before storage or authentication
citations: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet - Data Sanitization (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Keyboard form submission via Enter key
test_cases.defect_target: Forms requiring explicit mouse click on submit button because Enter key does not trigger form action
preconditions: Form containing multiple input fields and a submit action
steps: Fill valid values in all form fields using keyboard navigation
Focus a text input element
Press the Enter key (keyboard.press('Enter'))
Observe submission event
test_cases.expected_result: Pressing Enter triggers primary form submission equivalent to clicking the submit button, without requiring mouse interaction
citations: W3C WAI Web Accessibility Tutorials - Keyboard Operable Forms (https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/)

test_cases.name: Rapid double-click duplicate submission prevention
test_cases.defect_target: Creation of duplicate orders, duplicate charges, or multi-entity creation from rapid clicking on submit button
preconditions: State-modifying form (e.g. checkout, order placement, money transfer, comment post)
steps: Fill valid form details
Simulate 500ms network latency on target endpoint
Trigger rapid double-click on submit button within 50ms
Inspect network requests and database entity count
test_cases.expected_result: Submit button disables immediately upon first click with loading feedback, and exactly one entity is created on backend
test_cases.safety_constraints: Clean up created entity during teardown.
citations: Google web.dev - Sign-in form best practices (https://web.dev/articles/sign-in-form-best-practices)

test_cases.name: Server-side validation parity and field error display
test_cases.defect_target: Relying solely on client HTML5 validation, allowing invalid or malicious payloads when submitted directly via curl/API
preconditions: Form submission endpoint is reachable
steps: Construct HTTP POST request bypassing client-side browser validation
Send payload with missing required fields and invalid formats directly to API endpoint
Inspect HTTP status code and response body
test_cases.expected_result: Backend rejects request with HTTP 400 or 422, returns structured validation error objects matching frontend expectations, and does not perform database mutation
citations: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet - Server Side Validation (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Form input preservation on API submission failure
test_cases.defect_target: Form resetting and wiping all user-entered data when backend returns a validation error or network drops
preconditions: Form containing multiple text areas, inputs, and selections
steps: Fill in multiple form fields with substantial user text
Trigger a server-side error (e.g. by entering a duplicate title or simulating network failure)
Wait for error banner to appear
Inspect field values in DOM
test_cases.expected_result: Entered input values remain intact in their respective inputs so user does not need to retype everything; sensitive password fields may be cleared per security policy
citations: Google web.dev - Learn Forms: Usability (https://web.dev/learn/forms/)

test_cases.name: File upload validation for MIME type and file size
test_cases.defect_target: Unrestricted file upload accepting executable files (.exe, .sh), crashing on oversized files, or missing upload progress
preconditions: File upload feature exists in application
steps: Attempt to upload file exceeding maximum configured size (e.g. 25MB when limit is 5MB)
Attempt to upload disallowed file extension/MIME (e.g. script.sh or malformed.exe)
Attempt to upload valid allowed file (e.g. document.pdf or avatar.png)
test_cases.expected_result: Oversized file and disallowed types are rejected with clear user-friendly error messages before storage; valid file uploads successfully with upload feedback
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use benign dummy files for upload tests; clean up test uploads from bucket/disk.
citations: OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: CRUD lifecycle end-to-end consistency
test_cases.defect_target: Data loss, inability to update existing fields, or ghost records persisting after deletion
preconditions: User has permission to create, edit, and delete domain entities
steps: Create new entity with unique name and specific attributes (Create)
Query and verify entity attributes match created values (Read)
Modify an attribute (e.g. update status or description) and save (Update)
Verify updated attribute is reflected on refresh (Read updated)
Delete the entity (Delete)
Query entity again to verify it returns 404 or disappears from list
test_cases.expected_result: Full CRUD cycle completes with correct state transitions, updates persist across refetch, and deleted entity is completely removed or soft-deleted as designed
test_cases.safety_constraints: Perform lifecycle operations in test database or dedicated test tenant.
citations: Google SRE Book - Testing for Reliability (https://sre.google/sre-book/testing-reliability/)

test_cases.name: Mathematical and financial calculation precision
test_cases.defect_target: Floating-point rounding errors (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004), incorrect discount subtraction, or off-by-one tax calculations
preconditions: Module performing pricing, discounts, invoice totals, or measurements
steps: Execute calculation with known fractional values (e.g. price $19.99, discount 15%, tax 8.25%)
Test zero values (0% discount, $0 price)
Test 100% discount boundary
Compare computed result against exact decimal benchmark
test_cases.expected_result: All calculations match exact decimal precision, use round-half-up or standard currency conventions, and produce zero floating-point accumulation drift
test_cases.safety_constraints: Pure logic computation; zero environment risk.
citations: IEEE 754 Floating-Point Standards in Business Software

test_cases.name: Empty dataset zero-state presentation
test_cases.defect_target: Unhandled null/undefined pointer exception, blank page, or missing call to action when a list has zero records
preconditions: Authenticated test user with 0 created records in the collection (e.g. new account with 0 projects)
steps: Navigate to listing view (/projects, /orders, /notifications)
Wait for data fetch to complete
Inspect DOM for empty state container and action trigger
test_cases.expected_result: View renders a helpful empty state component (e.g. 'No projects yet') with a clear primary action button (e.g. 'Create your first project') and 0 console errors
test_cases.safety_constraints: Read-only test on clean user account.
citations: Google web.dev - UI State Management (https://web.dev/)

test_cases.name: Large dataset pagination and virtualization limits
test_cases.defect_target: Browser freeze, memory exhaustion, or database crash when loading tables with 1,000+ records
preconditions: Collection containing 500+ records seeded in test database
steps: Navigate to listing view
Verify default page size constraint is applied (e.g. 20 or 50 items per page)
Click next page, previous page, and direct page jump buttons
Inspect network payload size and DOM element count
test_cases.expected_result: Dataset paginates or virtualizes smoothly, DOM node count remains bounded (< 1500 nodes), page navigation updates data cleanly without lagging
test_cases.safety_constraints: Seed large test data in staging only; do not flood production databases.
citations: Google web.dev - Virtualize Large Lists (https://web.dev/articles/virtualize-large-lists-react-window)

test_cases.name: Search query and multi-filter combination idempotency
test_cases.defect_target: Inaccurate search matches, conflicting filter combinations returning empty erroneously, or search query parameters not syncing to URL
preconditions: Dataset with varied categories, statuses, and searchable text
steps: Type keyword into search field and press Enter
Verify results contain matching terms and URL query updates (?q=keyword)
Apply secondary filter (e.g. status=active, category=books)
Verify results satisfy both conditions simultaneously
Clear all filters
test_cases.expected_result: Filtering produces accurate intersection of selected criteria, clearing filters restores full collection, and URL search parameters stay synchronized
citations: Google Search Central - Filter and Facet Design Guidelines

test_cases.name: Timezone consistency and date serialization
test_cases.defect_target: Date shifting by one day across timezones, UTC mismatch, or invalid timestamp formatting
preconditions: Form or endpoint that accepts and stores date/time entries
steps: Configure client browser timezone to UTC-8 (PST)
Save record to backend
Switch browser timezone to UTC+9 (JST)
Reload record and inspect displayed date
test_cases.expected_result: Date is stored unambiguously in UTC or ISO-8601 with timezone offset, client renders intended local representation accurately, and no unintended date-shift occurs
citations: ISO 8601 Date and Time Representation Standards

test_cases.name: Optimistic UI update rollback on network or server error
test_cases.defect_target: Ghost state where UI shows an item deleted or liked, but server rejected the change, leaving client out of sync with database
preconditions: UI component implements optimistic updates (e.g. toggle favorite, delete card)
Network route interceptor configured to force HTTP 500 failure
steps: Trigger action (e.g. click 'Delete Item')
Observe immediate optimistic removal of item from UI
Mock network failure / HTTP 500 response from backend
Wait for client error handling
test_cases.expected_result: When server request fails, UI rolls back optimistic change, restores item in list, and displays an informative error toast alerting user of failure
citations: Playwright Network Mocking Guide (https://playwright.dev/docs/network)

test_cases.name: Concurrent modification and stale data conflict detection
test_cases.defect_target: Silent data overwrite (lost update problem) when two users or tabs edit the same record simultaneously
preconditions: Target entity with optimistic concurrency control (version column, ETag, or updated_at timestamp)
steps: Client A fetches record version 1
Client B fetches record version 1
Client A updates record, incrementing version to 2
Client B attempts to update record with outdated version 1
test_cases.expected_result: Backend rejects Client B's update with HTTP 409 Conflict, returns latest record state, and prevents silent overwrite of Client A's changes
citations: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics - Precondition Header Evaluation (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)

test_cases.name: Data isolation and tenant partition integrity
test_cases.defect_target: Tenant data leakage where Tenant A can view, search, or mutate Tenant B's confidential database records
preconditions: Tenant A and Tenant B exist with independent data records in same database schema
steps: Authenticate as Tenant A
Query listing endpoints and search APIs
Directly request Tenant B's entity ID via GET /api/entities/<tenant_b_id>
Attempt to update or delete Tenant B's entity via PUT /api/entities/<tenant_b_id>
test_cases.expected_result: Tenant A receives only Tenant A records in lists; direct queries to Tenant B records return HTTP 404 or 403; zero cross-tenant data is leaked
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use dedicated test organizations in staging.
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet - Multi-Tenant Authorization (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Anonymous access to designated public resources
test_cases.defect_target: Accidental lockdown of public marketing, documentation, pricing, or health check routes requiring authentication
preconditions: Anonymous client session (no headers or cookies)
steps: Navigate to public routes (/, /pricing, /about, /terms, /privacy)
Inspect HTTP status code and rendered content
test_cases.expected_result: All public routes return HTTP 200, render intended information, and do not redirect to login or show auth error dialogs
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Privileged route boundary enforcement for standard users
test_cases.defect_target: Standard authenticated user accessing administrative panels, user management, or billing routes
preconditions: Standard authenticated user account (role = 'user') exists
Privileged route exists (e.g. /admin, /admin/users)
steps: Log in as standard user
Attempt to navigate directly to /admin
Inspect router guard behavior and response
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation is intercepted, user is presented with HTTP 403 Forbidden view or redirected to standard /dashboard with clear permission notification, and zero admin controls or data are rendered
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet - Role-Based Access Control (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)
OWASP Top 10 A01:2021-Broken Access Control

test_cases.name: API endpoint authorization validation across roles
test_cases.defect_target: Backend API accepting privileged requests (e.g. POST /api/admin/system-reset) from unauthenticated users or standard users
preconditions: Admin endpoint exists (e.g. /api/admin/users)
Standard user token and anonymous client prepared
steps: Scenario A: Issue GET/POST to admin endpoint without authentication headers
Scenario B: Issue GET/POST to admin endpoint with standard user JWT
Inspect HTTP status codes
test_cases.expected_result: Scenario A returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized; Scenario B returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; backend does not execute the action or leak sensitive schema
citations: OWASP API Security Top 10 - Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) prevention
test_cases.defect_target: User A viewing, editing, or deleting User B's private invoices, documents, or personal data by changing ID in URL
preconditions: User A and User B both have private records (e.g. User A has Order 101, User B has Order 102)
steps: Authenticate as User A
Attempt to fetch User B's order: GET /api/orders/102
Attempt to modify User B's order: PUT /api/orders/102 with updated payload
Attempt to delete User B's order: DELETE /api/orders/102
test_cases.expected_result: All operations on User B's resource are rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found, and Order 102 remains unmodified in the database
test_cases.safety_constraints: Execute in test environment with test users.
citations: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021-Broken Access Control - Insecure Direct Object References
OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG-ATHZ-04)

test_cases.name: Role or permission revocation during active session
test_cases.defect_target: Stale JWT/session keeping revoked privileges active until token expiration, allowing a demoted or blocked user to continue admin actions
preconditions: Active administrator session in progress
Secondary session able to demote administrator account to standard user
steps: Log in as Admin User in Client 1
In backend/Client 2, update Admin User's role to 'standard_user'
From Client 1, trigger an administrative action (e.g. POST /api/admin/settings)
test_cases.expected_result: Administrative action is rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden immediately, or session is invalidated, ensuring revoked privileges take effect without waiting for long token expiry
citations: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet - Session Revocation (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Frontend UI control authorization parity
test_cases.defect_target: Hiding a delete or export button in UI for standard users while leaving the underlying API endpoint unprotected
preconditions: Feature with UI controls restricted by role (e.g. 'Delete Organization' button hidden from members)
steps: Log in as standard member in browser
Verify the restricted button is not rendered in the DOM
Extract underlying API endpoint for that action from source/network contract
Execute direct HTTP request to that endpoint using member's authentication token
test_cases.expected_result: Direct API request is rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden, proving UI hiding is backed by enforceable server-side access controls
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet - Defense in Depth (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Sensitive operation re-authentication confirmation
test_cases.defect_target: Allowing account deletion, email change, or password change without confirming current password, enabling CSRF/session hijack attacks
preconditions: Authenticated user session on account settings view
steps: Attempt to change email address or delete account without providing current password
Submit the request
Provide correct current password along with change request and submit
test_cases.expected_result: Operation is blocked when current password is omitted or invalid; operation completes only when current credentials are confirmed
citations: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet - Step-Up Authentication (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Cross-tenant boundary isolation and workspace separation
test_cases.defect_target: Tenant A admin accessing Tenant B's workspace administration, billing history, or members list
preconditions: Tenant A administrator and Tenant B workspace exist
steps: Log in as Tenant A administrator
Attempt to access Tenant B workspace URL (/workspaces/tenant-b/settings)
Attempt API calls with Tenant B workspace ID in headers or path
test_cases.expected_result: Access is completely denied with HTTP 403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found, and Tenant A cannot view or modify Tenant B workspace data
citations: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet - Multi-Tenant Authorization (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Happy-path API response schema and contract validation
test_cases.defect_target: Breaking frontend client assumptions due to missing properties, wrong data types, or unexpected null fields in API response
preconditions: API service is running with OpenAPI/Swagger spec or TypeScript interface contract
steps: Send valid requests to all primary endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
Validate HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204)
Validate JSON response schema against OpenAPI/JSON schema definitions
Verify all required fields exist with correct primitive types
test_cases.expected_result: Responses return HTTP 2xx, headers include Content-Type: application/json, and payloads conform strictly to schema contracts without undeclared field drops
citations: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.0 Contract Testing Standards

test_cases.name: HTTP 4xx client error presentation and formatting
test_cases.defect_target: Raw technical exceptions, cryptic codes, or empty response bodies when requests have client errors
preconditions: API endpoint accepting inputs
steps: Send malformed payload (invalid JSON syntax or missing required fields) -> expect 400 or 422
Send request without auth token -> expect 401
Send request with insufficient role -> expect 403
Send request for non-existent ID -> expect 404
test_cases.expected_result: API returns standardized error response (e.g. RFC 7807 Problem Details or consistent JSON object with error code, message, and details) without server stack traces
citations: RFC 7807 Problem Details for HTTP APIs (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807)

test_cases.name: HTTP 5xx server error resilience and UI error boundaries
test_cases.defect_target: Entire application crashing to a white screen when an API call returns 500 or 503
preconditions: Client application running in browser with network route interception available
steps: Intercept target data fetching endpoint and force HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
Observe UI component behavior and global error boundary
test_cases.expected_result: Component displays an isolated error fallback card with retry button, global navigation remains intact and interactive, and rest of page remains usable
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use client route mocking to simulate 500s safely.
citations: Playwright Network Guide - Modifying Responses (https://playwright.dev/docs/network)

test_cases.name: Request timeout and client cancellation handling
test_cases.defect_target: Indefinitely hanging loading spinners or frozen UI when backend or external service hangs
preconditions: Client API utility configured with timeout policy (e.g. 10s timeout)
steps: Mock API response to delay indefinitely (e.g. 30 seconds delay)
Trigger request from UI
Wait for configured timeout window to elapse
test_cases.expected_result: Request is aborted via AbortController after timeout, loading spinner dismisses, and user is shown an accessible timeout message with retry option
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use short mock timeouts (e.g. 2s) during automated test runs.
citations: Google SRE Book - Handling Overload and Deadlines (https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/)

test_cases.name: Network disconnection and offline recovery
test_cases.defect_target: Silent failure, missing user notification, or data loss when user loses network connectivity during use
preconditions: Application running in browser
steps: Simulate network offline via browser context (context.setOffline(true))
Attempt user action requiring network
Verify offline indicator / banner appears
Restore network connectivity (context.setOffline(false))
Trigger retry or verify auto-reconnect
test_cases.expected_result: Application displays accessible offline status banner, informs user changes cannot be synced offline, and successfully resumes functionality once connection is restored
citations: Playwright Network Guide - Offline Emulation (https://playwright.dev/docs/network)

test_cases.name: Malformed or empty JSON response defense
test_cases.defect_target: Unhandled JSON.parse exception or TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined crashing client
preconditions: Client application fetching data from API
steps: Intercept response and return empty body with HTTP 200
Intercept response and return malformed non-JSON HTML (e.g. gateway error HTML) with HTTP 200
Intercept response and return unexpected null payload
test_cases.expected_result: Client API wrapper catches JSON parsing failures defensively, falls back to error boundary, and reports friendly message without uncaught exception in console
citations: Google SRE Book - Defensive Programming Principles

test_cases.name: HTTP 429 Rate limiting and Retry-After compliance
test_cases.defect_target: Infinite retry storms hitting a rate-limited endpoint, or missing rate-limit warning in UI
preconditions: Rate limiter configured on API or mocked via response interceptor
steps: Send rapid burst of requests exceeding configured rate limit threshold
Inspect HTTP status code and response headers
Verify Retry-After header presence and value format
test_cases.expected_result: Server returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, includes Retry-After header, client halts automated retries, and UI displays clear rate-limit advisory
test_cases.safety_constraints: Run in isolated test environment; do not flood production endpoints.
citations: RFC 6585 Additional HTTP Status Codes - 429 Too Many Requests (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6585)
Google SRE Book - Addressing Cascading Failures (https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/)

test_cases.name: Third-party integration outage graceful degradation
test_cases.defect_target: Entire application failing because non-critical external third-party service (analytics, social widget, avatar service) is down
preconditions: Application integrates third-party service (e.g. Gravatar, Google Analytics, Sentry)
steps: Block network requests to external third-party domains (e.g. *.google-analytics.com, *.gravatar.com)
Navigate core user flows (login, view items, checkout, export)
Inspect application usability
test_cases.expected_result: Core application functionality remains 100% operational, graceful fallback occurs (e.g. default initials avatar rendered), and third-party block causes zero fatal errors
citations: Google SRE Book - Cascading Failures and Graceful Degradation (https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/)

test_cases.name: Missing environment variable detection during backend initialization
test_cases.defect_target: Backend starting silently with undefined environment variables and crashing during live user traffic on first database call
preconditions: Backend server startup script with environment configuration validator
steps: Simulate missing mandatory environment variable (e.g. unset DATABASE_URL or SECRET_KEY)
Attempt to start server process
Inspect exit code and standard error log
test_cases.expected_result: Application fails fast at startup with non-zero exit code, emits an explicit, actionable error message identifying the missing variable, and prevents starting in half-configured broken state
test_cases.safety_constraints: Execute in isolated subprocess; do not affect running services.
citations: 12-Factor App - Config (https://12factor.net/config)
Google SRE Launch Checklist - Configuration Testing (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Non-functional or dead button detection
test_cases.defect_target: Dead buttons, non-interactive visual cards masquerading as clickable buttons, or missing click handlers

steps: Scan all <button>, [role='button'], and interactive action elements on page
Verify each button has an attached click listener, type='submit', or programmatic event binding
Click primary action buttons and observe that an expected action (navigation, dialog, fetch, or state update) occurs
test_cases.expected_result: Every interactive control has a functional binding; no button produces a dead click without feedback or console error
citations: Google web.dev - Learn Accessibility: Interactive controls (https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/)

test_cases.name: Comprehensive view state verification (Loading, Empty, Success, Error)
test_cases.defect_target: Missing loading skeletons, absent empty states, or unstyled error flashes in async views
preconditions: Async data-driven component
steps: Verify Loading State: delay API response and verify skeleton or spinner is displayed
Verify Empty State: mock empty array response [] and verify empty state graphics/message render
Verify Success State: mock valid array response and verify records render correctly
Verify Error State: mock HTTP 500 error and verify error retry card renders
test_cases.expected_result: All 4 states (Loading, Empty, Success, Error) are fully styled, informative, and transition smoothly without layout jumps
citations: Google web.dev - Cumulative Layout Shift (https://web.dev/articles/cls)

test_cases.name: Unintended horizontal scrolling and layout overflow detection
test_cases.defect_target: Horizontal scrollbars breaking mobile layout, fixed-width elements overflowing document body
preconditions: Browser viewports set to 375px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1280px (desktop)
steps: For each viewport size, navigate to all primary views
Evaluate document.documentElement.scrollWidth vs window.innerWidth in JavaScript
Inspect whether horizontal scrollbar is present
test_cases.expected_result: document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth across all viewports; zero unintended horizontal overflow exists
citations: Google web.dev - Responsive web design basics (https://web.dev/articles/responsive-web-design-basics)

test_cases.name: Responsive layout adaptation across breakpoints
test_cases.defect_target: Overlapping columns, clipped text, broken grid containers, or unreadable typography at tablet/mobile breakpoints
preconditions: Application running in browser
steps: Resize browser viewport across standard breakpoints: 375x667, 768x1024, 1024x768, 1440x900
Verify navigation bar collapses to drawer on mobile and expands on desktop
Verify multi-column grids collapse to single-column on mobile without overlapping
Capture screenshots at each breakpoint
test_cases.expected_result: Layout reflows cleanly, text remains readable without clipping, interactive controls maintain touch targets (>= 44x44px), and columns stack properly
citations: Google web.dev - Accessible tap targets (https://web.dev/articles/accessible-tap-targets)

test_cases.name: Modal and dialog keyboard trapping and focus restoration

Verify modal opens and focus moves to first focusable element inside modal
Press Tab repeatedly to verify focus cycles only within the modal (focus trap)
Press Escape key to close modal
Verify modal closes and focus is restored to the original trigger button
test_cases.expected_result: Modal traps keyboard focus while open, Escape key dismisses modal, and closing modal returns focus accurately to trigger element
citations: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices - Dialog (Modal) Pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

test_cases.name: Image loading failure and fallback handling
test_cases.defect_target: Broken image icon, unstyled alt text breaking layout, or raw crash when an image URL returns 404
preconditions: Component displaying user avatars, product pictures, or thumbnails

Inspect DOM after image error event triggers
test_cases.expected_result: Component catches onError event and renders a designated fallback icon, placeholder SVG, or stylized initials avatar without broken image icons or layout shift
citations: Google web.dev - Optimize your images (https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp-images)

test_cases.name: Browser console error and unhandled exception inspection
test_cases.defect_target: Unhandled JavaScript errors, React hydration errors, missing key warnings, or 404 asset failures logged to console
preconditions: Browser session with console error listener attached
steps: Attach page.on('console', msg => if msg.type() == 'error': record(msg))
Attach page.on('pageerror', err => record(err))
Navigate through all documented primary user journeys (home, catalog, details, forms)
Inspect captured console message log
test_cases.expected_result: Zero uncaught page errors, zero framework hydration mismatches, and zero missing key warnings emitted to browser console
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Client-Side Error Monitoring (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Toast and notification deduplication and dismissibility
test_cases.defect_target: Toasts stacking endlessly on top of each other, covering interactive buttons, or failing to dismiss automatically
preconditions: Application using toast or snackbar notification system
steps: Trigger same user action twice in rapid succession (e.g. 'Saved draft')
Observe toast container in DOM
Verify toasts do not duplicate or stack identically
Click manual dismiss button (X) on toast
Wait for auto-dismiss timer to elapse on second toast
test_cases.expected_result: Duplicate toasts are debounced or deduplicated, manual dismiss closes toast immediately, and auto-dismiss timer removes notification smoothly after configured delay
citations: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices - Alert Pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)

test_cases.name: Form input focus visual feedback and error highlighting
test_cases.defect_target: Active input showing zero visual feedback, or invalid input indistinguishable from valid input
preconditions: Form inputs rendered on page
steps: Focus an input field and inspect CSS styles (outline, border-color, box-shadow)
Trigger a validation error on that field and inspect error styling
Verify contrast of focus ring and error ring
test_cases.expected_result: Focused field displays a distinct visible focus outline/ring with >= 3:1 contrast against adjacent background; invalid field changes border to error color and links to error message
citations: WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.7 Focus Visible (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/focus-visible.html)

test_cases.name: Full keyboard navigation without mouse pointer requirement
test_cases.defect_target: Keyboard traps, non-focusable interactive controls, or inability to complete user journeys without a mouse
preconditions: Application running in browser

Using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and Arrow keys, complete the journey from start to finish
Verify focus never gets trapped in an element with no way out
test_cases.expected_result: All interactive controls (links, buttons, inputs, dropdowns) are operable via keyboard alone; no keyboard traps exist (WCAG 2.1.2)
citations: W3C WCAG 2.1 Guideline 2.1 Keyboard Accessible (https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/#keyboard-accessible)

test_cases.name: Visible focus indicator preservation across interactive elements

Audit all interactive elements (:focus pseudo-class)
Verify each element has a visible outline, box-shadow, or color change when focused
test_cases.expected_result: No interactive element suppresses focus outlines without providing an accessible visible replacement; focus indicators achieve at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent background
citations: W3C WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/focus-visible.html)
Axe-core Rule: focus-visible

test_cases.name: Semantic HTML structure and heading hierarchy

Verify main content is wrapped in a <main> landmark

test_cases.name: Accessible names for buttons and icon controls

Flag any control where computed accessible name is empty or solely whitespace

W3C Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.1

test_cases.name: Form label association and error binding

test_cases.expected_result: Every form field is programmatically associated with a permanent label, and inline error messages are linked via aria-describedby with aria-invalid='true'
citations: W3C WCAG 2.1 SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)

test_cases.name: Alternative text for meaningful and decorative images
test_cases.defect_target: Meaningful images missing alt attribute, or decorative icons cluttering screen reader announcements with filename text
preconditions: Page containing and

Verify informative images have descriptive, non-redundant text (not 'image', 'picture', or filename)
Verify decorative icons have alt='' or aria-hidden='true'

citations: W3C WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/non-text-content.html)

test_cases.name: WCAG AA color contrast compliance for text and UI elements
test_cases.defect_target: Low-contrast grey text on white background or faint button text unreadable for users with low vision
preconditions: Page styles loaded in browser
steps: Run axe-core color contrast analysis on rendered view

Measure contrast ratio of large text (>= 18pt or bold >= 14pt, required: >= 3:1)
