test_cases.defect_target: Generic 'Vite App' or 'React App' titles, empty descriptions, or missing meta tags in search result snippets
preconditions: Public views rendered in browser
steps: Navigate to public pages (/, /about, /pricing, /blog)
Extract document.title and meta[name='description']
Verify title is non-empty, distinct per page, and does not contain placeholder default ('Vite App')
Verify description length is between 50 and 160 characters
test_cases.expected_result: Every public route possesses a unique descriptive page title and meaningful meta description
citations: Google Search Central - Control your titles and snippets in search results (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link)

test_cases.name: Canonical URL tag specification
test_cases.defect_target: Search engine indexing duplicate URLs for query variations or HTTP/HTTPS differences
preconditions: Public pages rendered in browser
steps: Inspect <link rel='canonical' href='...'> in document <head>
Verify canonical URL uses HTTPS and absolute domain
Verify query parameter variations point to the same canonical URL
test_cases.expected_result: Canonical link tag exists on all public routes, pointing to the authoritative URL without tracking parameters
citations: Google Search Central - Consolidate duplicate URLs (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)

test_cases.name: Robots.txt and sitemap.xml availability
test_cases.defect_target: Search crawlers receiving 404 on robots.txt or missing sitemap.xml to discover public content
preconditions: Web server running
steps: Fetch /robots.txt -> expect HTTP 200 with text/plain content
Fetch /sitemap.xml -> expect HTTP 200 with valid XML content
Verify sitemap lists active public routes and excludes private/admin paths
test_cases.expected_result: robots.txt and sitemap.xml are accessible, formatted correctly, and link crawlers to public content while disallowing sensitive internal routes
citations: Google Search Central - Robots.txt introduction (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro)

test_cases.name: Private route indexing prevention via noindex meta tag
test_cases.defect_target: Search engines indexing private user dashboards, admin screens, or password reset pages in public search results
preconditions: Private routes rendered in browser (/dashboard, /settings, /admin, /reset-password)
steps: Navigate to private authenticated routes
Inspect <meta name='robots'> tag in document <head>
Inspect X-Robots-Tag HTTP response headers
test_cases.expected_result: Private and sensitive routes include <meta name='robots' content='noindex, nofollow'> or X-Robots-Tag: noindex header to prevent crawler indexing
citations: Google Search Central - Block search indexing with noindex (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing)

test_cases.name: Social sharing OpenGraph and Twitter card metadata
test_cases.defect_target: Broken social share previews on Slack, Twitter/X, and LinkedIn displaying blank thumbnails and missing titles
preconditions: Public views rendered in browser
steps: Inspect meta tags in document <head> for:
property='og:title'
property='og:description'
property='og:image'
property='og:url'
name='twitter:card'
Verify og:image URL is absolute and returns HTTP 200
test_cases.expected_result: OpenGraph and Twitter card metadata tags exist with valid absolute image URLs, ensuring rich link previews when shared
citations: The Open Graph Protocol (https://ogp.me/)

test_cases.name: Structured data schema.org JSON-LD validity
test_cases.defect_target: Malformed JSON-LD syntax crashing crawlers or failing Google Rich Results validation
preconditions: Pages incorporating <script type='application/ld+json'>
steps: Extract all application/ld+json script tag contents from DOM
Parse JSON payload to verify valid syntax
Verify mandatory schema.org fields (@context, @type, name) are populated
test_cases.expected_result: JSON-LD scripts parse without JSON syntax errors and conform to schema.org entity specifications
citations: Google Search Central - Understand how structured data works (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)

test_cases.name: Semantic 404 HTTP status code for missing content
test_cases.defect_target: Soft 404s where missing content returns HTTP 200 with an error message, confusing search engine indexers
preconditions: Server rendering or SSR handling routes
steps: Request non-existent product or page URL (e.g. /products/item-does-not-exist)
Inspect HTTP status code returned by server
test_cases.expected_result: Server returns genuine HTTP 404 status code (not 200) alongside the user-friendly 404 page, preventing soft 404 crawler penalties
citations: Google Search Central - Soft 404 errors (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/http-network-errors)

test_cases.name: Cross-browser rendering consistency across major engines
test_cases.defect_target: Features working in Chromium but broken in WebKit (Safari) or Gecko (Firefox) due to vendor-specific APIs
preconditions: Playwright browser binaries installed for chromium, firefox, webkit
steps: Launch Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit browser instances
Execute primary user journey (navigate, fill form, toggle drawer) in each browser engine
Compare visual layout and console error outputs across engines
test_cases.expected_result: Application renders without visual breakage and user journeys complete successfully across all 3 browser engines
citations: Playwright Browsers Documentation (https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers)

test_cases.name: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) origin validation
test_cases.defect_target: CORS headers set to wildcard '*' with credentials, or unauthorized origin allowed to read private API responses
preconditions: API service handling cross-origin requests
steps: Send OPTIONS preflight request with Origin: https://evil.example
Inspect Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header
Send OPTIONS preflight request with approved origin: Origin: https://app.example
test_cases.expected_result: API rejects unauthorized origin (does not return matching Access-Control-Allow-Origin); approved origin returns explicit header; wildcards with credentials are strictly forbidden
citations: OWASP Cross-Origin Resource Sharing Cheat Sheet (https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Origin_Resource_Sharing_Cheat_Sheet.html)

test_cases.name: Mixed content blocking prevention over HTTPS
test_cases.defect_target: Images, scripts, or API endpoints requested over unencrypted http:// on an HTTPS page, blocked by browser
preconditions: Application loaded over HTTPS
steps: Monitor network requests during complete user session
Check for any subresource requests (scripts, styles, images, fetch) initiated with http:// protocol
test_cases.expected_result: 100% of subresource requests use https:// or relative paths; zero mixed-content warnings or blocked requests occur
citations: Google web.dev - What is mixed content? (https://web.dev/articles/what-is-mixed-content)

test_cases.name: Third-party script failure tolerance and isolation
test_cases.defect_target: External tag manager, font provider, or chat widget outage halting all client JavaScript execution
preconditions: Third-party scripts included via script tags
steps: Block external third-party script domains in browser context (e.g. cdn.thirdparty.com)
Reload page and test core interactions (click nav, open modal, submit form)
test_cases.expected_result: Page continues rendering without unhandled exception; core features function normally despite external script failure
citations: Google SRE Book - Cascading Failures (https://sre.google/sre-book/addressing-cascading-failures/)

test_cases.name: Cookie persistence across navigation and cross-site requests
test_cases.defect_target: Cookies disappearing due to incorrect Domain or Path attributes, causing random session drops
preconditions: Authenticated session with cookies
steps: Inspect Set-Cookie Domain and Path parameters
Navigate between subdomains or nested paths (e.g. /app to /account)
Verify cookies remain attached to outgoing fetch requests
test_cases.expected_result: Cookie Path and Domain parameters match application structure, maintaining session across all configured application routes
citations: MDN Web Docs - HTTP Cookies: Scope (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies)

test_cases.name: Global JavaScript unhandled rejection handler verification
test_cases.defect_target: Silent uncaught Promise rejections freezing UI without user notification or error tracking
preconditions: Application client bundle loaded
steps: Verify window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...) is registered in client entry point
Trigger a test unhandled promise rejection in console
Verify global handler catches rejection and logs or displays user-friendly advisory
test_cases.expected_result: Global unhandled rejection listener is active, captures asynchronous promise failures, and routes errors to telemetry without crashing window
citations: MDN Web Docs - Window: unhandledrejection event (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/unhandledrejection_event)

test_cases.name: Clean offline and slow-network fallback behavior
test_cases.defect_target: Blank screen on slow 2G connections, or broken asset caching in progressive web apps
preconditions: Browser session with network throttling configured
steps: Throttle network to Slow 3G (500kbps, 400ms RTT)
Navigate to application homepage
Observe rendering sequence and visual stability
test_cases.expected_result: Page displays initial HTML and styled loading skeleton within 3 seconds, assets load progressively, and no network timeout occurs
citations: Google web.dev - Fast load times on slow networks (https://web.dev/articles/reliable)

test_cases.name: Structured application logging format verification
test_cases.defect_target: Unstructured plain text logs impossible to query in log aggregators (Datadog, CloudWatch, GCP Logging)
preconditions: Backend server log output stream available
steps: Trigger standard HTTP request to server
Capture emitted log line from stdout
Parse log line as JSON
test_cases.expected_result: Log entries are valid JSON containing standard fields: timestamp (ISO 8601), level (INFO/WARN/ERROR), message, and request context
citations: 12-Factor App - Logs (https://12factor.net/logs)
Google SRE Book - Monitoring Distributed Systems (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

test_cases.name: Request and correlation ID propagation across services
test_cases.defect_target: Unable to trace an error reported by a customer through frontend to backend microservices and database
preconditions: API service handling incoming requests
steps: Send HTTP request with header 'X-Request-ID: test-req-12345'
Inspect response headers for 'X-Request-ID'
Inspect server log emitted for that request
test_cases.expected_result: Server echoes X-Request-ID in response headers, generates one if missing, and includes the ID in all server log entries for that request
citations: W3C Trace Context Specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/)

test_cases.name: Centralized error monitoring and telemetry capture
test_cases.defect_target: Production exceptions occurring invisibly without alerting the engineering team
preconditions: Error monitoring client (e.g. Sentry, Datadog) configured in application
steps: Trigger controlled test exception in test environment
Verify error reporting client captures exception with stack trace, release version, and environment tag
test_cases.expected_result: Exception is captured and dispatched to telemetry collector with full stack trace and metadata, without crashing client session
test_cases.safety_constraints: Use designated test DSN in staging.
citations: Google SRE Book - Monitoring Distributed Systems (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

test_cases.name: Key operational metrics instrumentation (Latency, Traffic, Errors, Saturation)
test_cases.defect_target: Operating blind in production with no visibility into requests-per-second, 5xx error rates, or p95 response times
preconditions: Metrics endpoint (e.g. /metrics) or telemetry exporter configured
steps: Fetch metrics endpoint (/metrics)
Verify Prometheus or OpenTelemetry metric format
Verify Four Golden Signals are tracked: latency histogram, request counter, error counter, and active worker saturation
test_cases.expected_result: Metrics endpoint returns valid metric time-series data covering request count, latency percentiles, and error counters
citations: Google SRE Book - The Four Golden Signals (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/)

test_cases.name: Post-deployment smoke test suite execution
test_cases.defect_target: Deployment declared successful while production is returning 500s or serving blank pages
preconditions: Target environment URL available post-deployment
steps: Execute automated smoke script hitting /health, public homepage, and API version endpoint
Verify all smoke endpoints return HTTP 200 within 5 seconds of deployment completion
test_cases.expected_result: Post-deployment smoke suite passes 100%, providing positive automated confirmation that the release is serving live traffic correctly
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Post-Launch Smoke Testing (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Rollback trigger criteria and threshold definition
test_cases.defect_target: Teams arguing or hesitating during an outage because objective rollback criteria were never defined
preconditions: Deployment and rollback documentation
steps: Verify documented rollback trigger criteria exist: e.g. error rate > 1% over 3 minutes, or p95 latency > 2000ms for 5 minutes, or smoke test failure
Verify rollback command or automated CD rollback trigger is documented and tested
Confirm previous deployment artifact is retained for immediate rollback
test_cases.expected_result: Objective, measurable rollback criteria are documented, previous release artifact is verified available, and rollback path is clearly established
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Rollback Plans (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)

test_cases.name: Critical failure alerting rule coverage
test_cases.defect_target: System outages going unnoticed for hours due to missing alerts on high error rate or health check failure
preconditions: Alerting configuration (e.g. Prometheus rules, Datadog monitors, CloudWatch alerts)
steps: Audit alerting rules for coverage of:
1. Continuous health check probe failures
2. HTTP 5xx error rate spike (> 2% of total traffic)
3. Elevated p95/p99 response latency
Verify alert destination (e.g. Slack channel, PagerDuty, email) is configured
test_cases.expected_result: Alerting rules are active for critical outage indicators with actionable paging destinations
citations: Google SRE Book - Being On-Call and Alerting (https://sre.google/sre-book/being-on-call/)

test_cases.name: Release verification confirmation report generation
test_cases.defect_target: Releasing code without recording what was verified, leaving no audit trail of test results or accepted risks
preconditions: Verification run completed
steps: Aggregate all check results across catalog categories
Format standardized Production Readiness Verification Report
Classify each check into PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT_RUN, NOT_APPLICABLE, MANUAL_REVIEW, UNKNOWN
Document known residual risks, workload assumptions, and sign-off recommendation
test_cases.expected_result: Comprehensive readiness report is generated and archived, clearly distinguishing verified facts from assumptions, with zero unsubstantiated claims
citations: Google SRE Launch Checklist - Launch Review (https://sre.google/sre-book/launch-checklist/)
